summary: Exactly 40 feature contracts, six pilot families and the four incumbent C0 owners. All formulas are candidate designs or explicitly constrained benchmarks. No empirical discovery or policy activation is claimed.

P1.name: Attention with measured execution-quality controls
P1.primary_endpoint: Next 30-minute exact underlying log high/low range after eligible consumer admission; B2-RI versus B1-RI squared loss under the accepted v1 specification. Exact boundary labels are required; unsigned activity has no bullish interpretation.
P1.population: Dynamic causally admitted and prequalified incumbent US-common-stock buy pool under the accepted v1 population rule; exact historical revisions required, never current constituents substituted for history.

P2.name: Signed dollar delta with matched-package ambiguity
P2.primary_endpoint: Next 30-minute underlying market/sector-residual log return; B2-RI versus B1-RI squared loss under the exact as-of residual-label and causal-clock rules in the accepted v1 specification. Package/unknown/quality qualifications and diagnostics remain required.
P2.population: Dynamic causally admitted and prequalified incumbent US-common-stock buy pool under the accepted v1 population rule; exact historical revisions required, never current constituents substituted for history.

P3.name: ATM IV minus square-root physical-variance forecast
P3.primary_endpoint: QLIKE of the fixed positive B2-RI variance forecast versus B1-RI over the next 20 NYSE sessions at the same consumer clock, against matched ACT/365F realized variance. The accepted specification fixes the mapping; the possibly negative OIF19 residual is never itself a variance forecast.
P3.variance_forecast_mapping_gate: The exact positive multiplicative B2-RI mapping, beta domain, convex solver, training-only scaler and finite-value/refusal rules are fixed in PILOT_STUDY_SPEC_V1.md section 4, with the fixed B1-RI target adapter in Appendix A. beta=0 exactly recovers B1-RI; no second smear, clipping or failed-row fallback. QLIKE scores positive variance forecasts against nonnegative matched ACT/365F realized variance, including zero, never the signed OIF19 residual. Mapping choice is no longer an open design gate; causal historical forecast/snapshot receipts, fit qualification, owner acceptance and sealed empirical registration remain required. This is engineering acceptance, not fitted or empirically validated forecasting.
P3.population: Dynamic causally admitted and prequalified incumbent US-common-stock buy pool under the accepted v1 population rule; exact historical revisions required, never current constituents substituted for history.

P4.name: Carry-adjusted matched IV spread
P4.primary_endpoint: Five-session market/sector-residual log return after a one-session skip from eligible Friday formation; B2-RI versus B1-RI squared loss under the accepted v1 specification. Borrow-observed, low-fee and missing-borrow cohorts remain explicit.
P4.population: Dynamic causally admitted and prequalified incumbent US-common-stock buy pool under the accepted v1 population rule; exact historical revisions required, never current constituents substituted for history.

P5.name: Explicit scenario hedge stress
P5.primary_endpoint: Numerical qualification first, then next 10-minute ACT/365F realized-variance QLIKE for the one fixed OIF13 inventory/shock augmentation versus B1-RI. Scenario alternatives are diagnostics; unknown dealer inventory and absent genuine incumbent ETF covariates prohibit stronger claims or invented forecasts.

P6.name: Executable contract quality
P6.primary_endpoint: Observed 60-second full-fill implementation-shortfall MAE, B2-RI versus B1-RI, strictly conditional on actual complete fills and independently observed fees. Exact target, side/quantity/deadline, fit and missing/no-fill handling are fixed by the accepted v1 specification. Coverage and simulated hedged markouts are diagnostics; no actual-fill or cost-calibration result can be supplied by self-generated simulation.

model_definitions.variance_units: RVar means realized variance; RVol=sqrt(RVar). Annualization and horizon are explicit and matched. Vega nu=dV/d(decimal sigma) is measured per quoted price unit; multiply by q*m and by 0.01 for a one-volatility-point contract-dollar sensitivity. For P3, annualized RVar_H divides the integrated squared-return sum by actual matched T_H on ACT/365F; a 252/n series requires the explicit conversion in physical_variance_forecast. sqrt(E[RVar_H]) must not be described as E[RVol_H].
model_definitions.portfolio_and_hedge_units: q*m*Gamma*S^2*0.01 is the gamma-driven component of portfolio delta-notional sensitivity for a 1% spot move. It is not the full derivative of S*Delta: d(S*Delta)/dS=Delta+S*Gamma. Positive signed h*m Greek sensitivities describe the assumed option portfolio; a delta-neutral hedge adjustment has the opposite sign. OIF13/14/15/32 explicitly include the hedge minus sign. OIF13 uses endpoint hedge notional at S_star=S_0+δS, with positive values denoting modeled underlying purchases; path cash is excluded. Linear Greek hedge approximations remain reference-spot sensitivities and are rescaled by S_star/S_0 when compared with endpoint target notional. OIF32 is pure time aging with unchanged spot, so reference and endpoint spot coincide.
model_definitions.scenario_interpretation: Full repriced hedge changes can indicate pro-cyclical or counter-cyclical hedge demand under the named inventory and surface assumptions. They do not demonstrate actual dealer trading, market price impact, causal volatility effects or the probability of a scenario.
model_definitions.contract_model: M is a qualified price/IV-inversion model with the actual exercise style, deliverable, dated dividends, rate curve and declared borrow treatment. European reference cases and American/tree cases are qualified separately. IV inputs use valid quote midpoint unless a feature explicitly names trade price. Price target, underlying feed, IV convention and Greek finite-difference scale are versioned.

model_definitions.signing_rule: A print is eligible only if its correction/condition policy is qualified, canonical identity is valid, quote was strictly earlier and available, 0<=bid<ask, both sizes positive, bid<=p<=ask, quote age is within the preregistered feed/root threshold, and package/order ambiguity is absent under the named policy. On that subset a=sign(p-(bid+ask)/2); exact midpoint => a=0 unknown. All ineligible prints have a=0 plus reasons and remain in coverage/mass accounting. This conservative rule does not establish actual customer direction, opening state or counterparties.

maturity_buckets.M0: known payoff fixing in current trading session; still tradable, positive remaining time
maturity_buckets.M1: positive remaining time through 7 calendar days, excluding M0

model_definitions.surface_interpolation: For a fixed forward-moneyness location, bracket with eligible strikes and expiries; interpolate total variance W=T*sigma^2 linearly in log(K/F) and then in T. sigma(T)=sqrt(W(T)/T). Forward ATM is K=F under the declared carry model. Solve signed spot-delta targets using the same model; do not extrapolate. Positive variance, shape/arbitrage diagnostics and bid/ask inversion sensitivity are retained.

physical_variance_forecast.formation: 09:35 ET is the scheduled snapshot slot on eligible full-session dates. Actual t is the first eligible consumer decision mark after artifact delivery; H is the same wall-clock timestamp 20 trading sessions later using the known exchange calendar. Input snapshot time never substitutes for consumer availability.
physical_variance_forecast.outcome: RVar_H=(sum_j r_j^2)/T_H, where T_H=(H-t in actual elapsed seconds)/(365*86400). Use qualified five-minute returns inside [t,H] plus each overnight close-to-open return once; partial endpoint intervals align to actual consumer decision and horizon timestamps. No future RVar enters a feature before H and acquisition maturity.
physical_variance_forecast.regressors: X=(1, log z_1, log mean(z_last5), log mean(z_last22), number of already-scheduled qualifying events in [t,H]); z_d is UNANNUALIZED completed-session integrated variance including its overnight return once. Require positive inputs; event types fixed before evaluation.
physical_variance_forecast.fit: OLS log(RVar_H)=X beta+epsilon on last 500 eligible training dates, minimum 252, with labels matured and purged before fit cutoff. Set smear=mean_train(exp(residual)); vhat_P,H=exp(X_current beta)*smear is a candidate conditional-mean RVar_H forecast. Freeze coefficients/smear during evaluation.
physical_variance_forecast.boundary: Log-HAR/smearing is a candidate positive forecasting design, not a reproduced academic coefficient or asserted calibrated physical distribution.
physical_variance_forecast.estimand: vhat_P,H targets E[RVar_H | information_available_at_t]. sqrt(vhat_P,H) estimates the square root of that expected variance, not E[sqrt(RVar_H) | information] and not expected realized volatility.
physical_variance_forecast.annualization: Implied sigma and physical RVar_H must share the actual matched ACT/365F horizon/year basis. If an external realized-variance series is annualized as (252/n)*sum(r^2) for the SAME return interval, convert to ACT/365F variance by multiplying it by (n/252)/T_H; equivalently convert its volatility by sqrt((n/252)/T_H). Without the interval, n and annualization metadata, the comparison is unavailable. No unconverted 252/n quantity may be subtracted from calendar-year IV variance.

QLIKE scores positive variance forecasts against nonnegative matched ACT/365F realized variance, including zero, never the signed OIF19 residual. Mapping choice is no longer an open design gate; causal historical forecast/snapshot receipts, fit qualification, owner acceptance and sealed empirical registration remain required. This is engineering acceptance, not fitted or empirically validated forecasting.

borrow_projection.regressors: X_fee=(1,b,b^2,Tbar,I_div,Spr_pair,log(F/S)); b is observed annual borrow fee decimal, Tbar OI-weighted remaining years, I_div known dividend before expiry, Spr_pair mean relative paired/wing quote spread as appropriate. All inputs are available at formation.
borrow_projection.fit: For each declared raw IV feature y, OLS y=X_fee beta+epsilon on last 500 eligible training daily 15:30 formations, minimum 252. Use fixed root/liquidity training scope; freeze beta in evaluation. Feature is y-X_fee beta.
borrow_projection.coverage: Borrow more than one trading session old or absent makes the adjusted feature unavailable. Raw, adjusted, low-fee and missing-fee cohorts remain visible; low-fee cutoff is chosen on training before evaluation.
borrow_projection.boundary: Rates/dividends/exercise are already handled consistently by the pricing model. This conditional projection is a candidate statistical borrow adjustment; it does not prove fees explain causally all price differences or that residuals are information.

shared_evaluation_contract.baseline: Accepted v1 engineering comparison: B2-RI versus B1-RI, the fixed target-trained adapter of a small causal incumbent-information summary, with the exact options-free-input B0 comparator and lineage audit. P1-P4 use the dynamic causally consumer-admitted US-common-stock buy pool and fixed qualifications; retain full eligible/failed census, revision/population identity and selection lineage. B0 inputs do not make the options-conditioned cohort options-free. P5/P6 retain distinct declared populations and require genuine incumbent covariate receipts for forecasting. The wider actual-production-policy/all-information incrementality goal remains separate and unsatisfied by any RI result. Exact definitions are in PILOT_STUDY_SPEC_V1.md and pilot-study-spec.v1.json.
shared_evaluation_contract.design: Follow the accepted v1 specification for labels, price sampling, units, clocks, training-only transforms, nested as-of/held-out B0 and B1-RI offsets, mature-label purging, losses, screening margins, deterministic bootstrap/power rules and typed refusals. Source/dataset/date/owner/power and empirical-registration bindings remain unaccepted. No extra model, horizon, transform or feature search is authorized. Controls remain required qualifications/diagnostics; a positive RI result is not automatically fully confounder-adjusted private information.
shared_evaluation_contract.multiplicity: Exactly six v1 primary hypotheses, Holm familywise .05 with blocked/unrun/invalid p=1, under the frozen specification. Its exact dependence, resampling, intervals, fixed power simulation and minimum-20-primary-calendar-block planning rules apply; these are not power proof or exact finite-sample guarantees. Queued variants do not become extra primaries. Prior #8286 BH results retain their original family.
shared_evaluation_contract.prior_evidence: OA-2R/Macro #8286 is completed historical work: 60 evaluable cells, three within-family BH rejections reported, no repeat across all three eras, and historical alpha unvalidated. PIT provenance, fresh out-of-sample evidence and executable economics remain unproven. Exact-feature equivalence requires a trial fingerprint; these newly explicit variants do not erase or automatically inherit old statistics.
shared_evaluation_contract.authority: No score activation, ranking, trade recommendation, admission veto, sizing, deployment or new operational state transition follows from this catalog.
shared_evaluation_contract.classification_validation: Selectively reviewed labels cannot establish population precision or calibrated directional confidence. Any such estimate needs a prespecified held-out/random or properly weighted label sample, coverage and venue/condition limits.
shared_evaluation_contract.economics_validation: Quoted markouts and simulated spread/fee scenarios provide diagnostics and rejection/stress tests, not self-validation of execution costs. Positive realized-fill, cost or economic-performance claims require independently observed execution/fee evidence or a qualified external empirical benchmark; do not validate a simulation by reusing its own assumed cost model.

L01.title: Option Volume and Stock Prices: Evidence on Where Informed Traders Trade
L01.access: Primary publisher abstract; full text not retrieved
L01.sample: Historical intraday equity/options observations; exact dates and selection criteria were not verified from accessible primary text.
L01.horizon: Intraday lead–lag relations; exact lag grid not verified.
L01.definition: Directional option-volume categories distinguish bullish combinations (call buys/put sales) from bearish combinations (put buys/call sales).

L02.title: The Information in Option Volume for Future Stock Prices
L02.access: Full published paper retrieved; targeted methods and results reviewed
L02.sample: CBOE non-market-maker volume, January 1990–December 2001; actual buy/sell, opening/closing, and investor-type categories.
L02.horizon: Next trading day and next week, with subsequent decay examined.
L02.definition: Buyer-opening puts divided by buyer-opening puts plus calls; daily cross-sectional quintiles.

L03.title: Volatility Information Trading in the Option Market
L03.access: Full published paper retrieved; targeted methods and results reviewed
L03.horizon: Individual future trading days at lags 1–5.
L03.definition: Sum of signed call and put contracts weighted by vega/option price, approximating the derivative of log option price with respect to volatility; baseline maturities exceed one week.

L04.title: The option to stock volume ratio and future returns
L04.access: Full published paper downloaded from author-hosted PDF; targeted sections reviewed
L04.sample: 1996–2010; 611,173 firm-weeks combining OptionMetrics, CRSP and Compustat.
L04.horizon: Skip one trading day, then measure the following five trading days.
L04.definition: Weekly option contracts across strikes, expiring within the 30-trading-day window beginning five days after trade, divided by equity volume in 100-share lots.

L05.title: Why does the option to stock volume ratio predict stock returns?
L05.access: Primary institutional abstract and indexed publisher excerpts; full text not retrieved
L05.sample: ISE Open/Close Trade Profile observations; exact sample dates were not verified from accessible primary text.
L05.horizon: Weekly stock-return predictability; precise skip/formation convention requires full-text verification.
L05.definition: Decomposition of relative volume into signed opening/closing transaction categories.

L06.title: Deviations from Put-Call Parity and Stock Return Predictability
L06.access: Published abstract plus full March 2007 working-paper version; final tables not retrieved
L06.sample: Earlier draft: January 1996–December 2005. Do not assume every final-paper filter matches this version.
L06.definition: Open-interest-weighted call-minus-put implied volatility for matched strike/expiration pairs.

L07.title: What Does the Individual Option Volatility Smirk Tell Us About Future Equity Returns?
L07.access: Full author-hosted accepted manuscript retrieved; targeted sections reviewed
L07.sample: January 1996–December 2005, OptionMetrics with equity, fundamentals and earnings data.
L07.horizon: Weekly formation with a one-day skip; persistence beyond the next week is examined.
L07.definition: IV of an OTM put with K/S in 0.80–0.95 minus an ATM call with K/S in 0.95–1.05; choose contracts closest to 0.95 and 1.00, respectively; 10–60 calendar days to expiration.

L08.title: Expected Stock Returns and Variance Risk Premia
L08.access: Full published paper retrieved; targeted methods and results reviewed
L08.horizon: Monthly through multi-year, with strongest principal evidence around one quarter.
L08.definition: Squared 30-day VIX minus preceding-month realized variance constructed from five-minute returns; both terms are observable at formation time. A forecast-based physical-variance alternative is also studied.

L09.title: Tails, Fears, and Risk Premia
L09.access: Full published paper retrieved; targeted methods and results reviewed
L09.sample: High-frequency S&P futures, 1990–2008; index options, 1996–2008. Baseline estimation through June 2007 is applied to the later crisis interval.
L09.horizon: Risk-premium decomposition and state variation, rather than a single next-day forecast target.
L09.definition: Physical jump-tail estimates from high-frequency returns compared with risk-neutral tails from short-maturity deep-OTM option prices.

L10.title: Is there price discovery in equity options?
L10.access: Primary abstracts and indexed publisher methods passages; full text not retrieved
L10.sample: Tick-level quotes for 36 liquid U.S. stocks and three ETFs, April 17, 2003–October 18, 2006 (882 trading days), verified in indexed publisher text.
L10.definition: Disagreement between stock prices and option-implied stock prices from matched call/put quotes.

L11.access: Detailed primary publisher abstract; full text not retrieved

L11.horizon: Trade classification, not a return forecast.
